revisionHistory.summary: First executable candidate for direction-a: a fixed sidebar, the shipped resource list absorbed as the console home, a resource detail page with an operator-only danger zone, and the domains and billing sections.
retainedTraits: the sealed anatomy of the shipped /provisioning list, unchanged
rejectedTraits: a component layout taking the routed body - LAYOUT-8 refuses `children` on one, and renaming the slot to `content` would satisfy only the lint
a count beside each sidebar section - NavLink has no count slot and nivo-backend has no count query
an invented machine size and an invented $0.00 - both are shown as unreadable
revisionHistory.reason: built from the plan record's selected direction; no feedback pass yet

revisionHistory.summary: Coverage completed and the danger zone given weight. Three states that 1.0 could not evidence are now rendered, and the destructive actions stopped looking like ordinary ones.
retainedTraits: every owner, contract, prop and word from 1.0 in the light desktop states that already existed
rejectedTraits: the danger zone drawn as an ordinary label-row-over-card - two presses that destroy data looked exactly as harmless as a save, with the warning trailing the heading on a shared baseline
a loading detail page with no title row at all - the whole screen jumped downward when the name arrived
`not-applicable` as a stand-in for `not yet photographed` - 1.0 used it for mobile, dark and the detail's own loading state, which are all real and all now rendered
revisionHistory.reason: The owner asked for 1.1 rather than approving 1.0 with three unevidenced states. The coverage pass then found two defects that only a capture could have found.
revisionHistory.visibleDifference: The danger zone now sits on its own bounded ground with the warning on a full line of its own. Everything else in the light desktop states is unchanged.

revisionHistory.summary: The target map declares what Apply actually does to the shipped route, and what becomes of the owner it replaces. Nothing on screen changed.
retainedTraits: every owner, contract, prop, state, tone and word from 1.1 - all 45 captures are unchanged
rejectedTraits: a sealed record that leaves `apps/app/src/app/provisioning/page.tsx` undeclared - the route exists and its import changes from ProvisioningPage to ResourcesPage, which the Apply gate correctly reported as an undeclared substitution
shipping ResourcesPage beside ProvisioningPage - two page owners drawing the identical screen, with nothing saying which one the route uses
revisionHistory.reason: verify_apply_materialization.mjs run before any write reported one substituted target. The Apply law is explicit that an undeclared edit returns to Preview rather than being written and explained afterwards - the third time this case pattern appeared, and each time it was the target map rather than the design.
revisionHistory.visibleDifference: None. Only the record's declarations changed.

parityBaseline.retained: The resource list keeps titled-summary-filter-over-body-page, FleetRow, the kind filter, the counter strip and all four states. The console adds a sidebar around it and a detail route below it.

evidence.claim: next build --webpack exited 0; 13 routes prerendered as a static export.
npx eslint on the candidate source exited 0 under the full canon rule set.
the console frame draws one nav and one main; the sidebar marks the current section from the path.
the operator state renders the danger zone; the customer state does not render it at all.
the suspended workspace shows chart version and AI spend as unreadable rather than as zero.
rebuild/reprovision/wipe are operator-only HTTP endpoints; every core GraphQL query is scoped to the viewer.

unknowns: Whether the console home stays /provisioning or becomes /resources. The candidate targets the shipped route so the address a customer may hold does not change.
Where creditBurnUsd belongs. It is on the resource detail page and deliberately absent from billing, because an account-level total would silently exclude every agent workspace.
Whether the sidebar earns per-section counts before counts-by-status exists.
An operator reading another account's resource is not possible today - there is no operator READ surface at all - so the operator state renders that reader's OWN resource.

findings.severity: real defect, and it is in the PARITY BASELINE rather than in anything this case added
findings.summary: `identity-kind-status-action-row` is `flex-row` with no `flex-wrap` and no responsive variant. At 390px the name column shrinks to min-w-0 but two badges plus a button still need roughly 200px, so the row runs past the right edge and the primary action is cut off.
findings.evidence: resources-populated-mobile.png. The sidebar stacks correctly, so the console frame is not the cause.
findings.whyItWasNeverSeen: The shipped /provisioning page carries the same row and was sealed at 1280x900 only. Nobody photographed it at a phone width, including this session during the provisioning case.
findings.whyItIsNotFixedHere: How the row behaves at 390px is a product decision - wrap the badges under the name, drop the kind badge, or scroll the row - and Preview does not take product decisions. It returns to Plan, and it affects a screen that is already in production.

findings.severity: leaf defect, worked around and named
findings.summary: `Heading` sets resting classes when `isLoading` is true but renders `props.content ?? ""`. An empty element collapses, so a loading page had no title row at all and the whole screen jumped downward when the name arrived. `Text` solved the identical problem by rendering a non-breaking space; `Heading` was never given it.
findings.evidence: detail-loading.png before the workaround: the heading row was entirely absent.
findings.whyItIsNotFixedHere: packages/ui/src/leaves/Heading is outside this phase's write boundary. The page passes a non-breaking space while loading and says so at the call site; the leaf fix is recorded as a vocabulary proposal.

decisions.decision: Preview's write boundary was widened to packages/ui/src/contracts/index.ts
decisions.tradeoff: deviates from CONTEXT-LOCK-6, which makes Preview artifact-only; taken because Tree imports contractSpec statically, so a candidate-local registry would have meant copying Tree and proving that a facsimile renders

decisions.decision: the main landmark is opened by the frame rather than by each page
decisions.tradeoff: a page can no longer choose to be something other than main; taken because the shipped /provisioning page has zero main elements today and a per-page rule is one a page eventually forgets

decisions.decision: `$content` was replaced in label-row-over-card's body slot
decisions.tradeoff: widens a shared contract; taken because $content is not a ContractKey, so the slot resolved to `never` and no caller could ever have filled it

decisions.decision: the destructive presses carry no danger tone
decisions.tradeoff: the warning sentence carries all the weight; taken because the Button leaf has no danger variant and inventing a class in a block is refused

files.note: the framework boundary AND the console frame. It receives children and closes them into the `page` leaf immediately (LAYOUT-1); ConsoleNav is its sibling, never its parent.
the layout. Resolves which section is current from the path itself and takes nothing from the body (LAYOUT-2/3/8).
the console home; the shipped /provisioning page absorbed with its sealed anatomy intact.
one resource. Reading order is failure, then instruction, then facts, then danger.
domains, ordered by expiry, with days-remaining computed rather than read from a column nothing writes.
connected half: resolves the four words and renders only its twin.
drawing half. Renderable from a fixture, which is what the split protects.
MERGE, not overwrite: the console, resources, resourceDetail, domains and billing namespaces are added to the app's existing catalogue. Their English twins go to en.json.
stand-in until myExpertSite/myExpertSiteDeployment are wired. null values are REAL absences.
stand-in for myDomains, myWallet and myInvoices.
the console home route. It mounts the page and nothing else.
